title: Clitic Pronouns Cluster
text:
Participating projects
This cluster brings together projects

P06 - The (Non-)Deficiency and (Non-)Redundancy of Clitic Pronouns,
P07 - Deficiency and Redundancy in Iberoromance Pronominal Systems,
P08 - Fading Referene - The Pragmaticalization of Pronoun + Verb,
P09 - Animacy Feattures and the Flexibility of Pronouns.



Description
The Clitic Pronouns cluster brings together work on clitic systems and related grammatical phenomena across the participating subprojects. Its activities are focused on reading groups and have been closely connected to the Romance cluster, allowing the projects involved to coordinate analyses and empirical work where clitic pronouns intersect with broader questions concerning Romance grammar.

title: Zero Elements Cluster
text:
Participating projects

P03 - Mismatches in Binding and Coreference,

P08 - Fading Reference - The Pragmaticalization of Pronoun + Verb,

Description
The Zero Elements cluster brings together research on structures in which linguistic material is absent, omitted, or not overtly realized. Its activities have been closely linked to the Romance cluster, reflecting substantial overlap in the empirical domains investigated by the participating projects, such as null or zero pronominal elements and ellipsis phenomena.

title: Romance Data Cluster
text:
Participating projects
This cluster brings together projects

P06 - The (Non-)Deficiency and (Non-)Redundancy of Clitic Pronouns,
P07 - Deficiency and Redundancy in Iberoromance Pronominal Systems,
P08 - Fading Reference - The Pragmaticalization of Pronoun + Verb,

Description
The Romance Data cluster focuses on collaborative empirical work across Romance languages and varieties. A central activity has been a data-sharing initiative designed to facilitate access to relevant empirical materials across subprojects, alongside coordinated experimental work. One concrete outcome of this collaboration is a cross-Romance experiment on null objects across eight Romance varieties, involving subprojects P01, P06, P07, and P09 and extending cooperation beyond the immediate cluster.

title: Corpus and Annotation Cluster
text:
Participating projects

P02 - Grammatical Gender in Discourse,
P07 - Deficinecy and Redundancy in Iberoromance Pronominal Systems,
P08 - Fading Reference - The Pragmaticalization of Pronoun + Verb.



Description
The Corpus and Annotation cluster has produced a repository of corpora for Romance languages, covering Spanish and Italian and, to a more limited extent, Portuguese and Catalan. It functions as a network used for consultation between projects working with both custom and existing corpora. The repository provides descriptions of the individual corpora together with access links where available, creating a shared resource for corpus-based research across the project network.

title: P02 – Grammatical Gender in Discourse and Grammar
text:
Project description
Subproject 2 is interested in an analysis of the discourse structural interpretation of gender features. The main focus of the subproject is the study of gender mismatches, which describe cases where grammatical gender does not agree with semantic gender (e.g., in German “das Mädchen”, where a neuter determiner is used in an expression referring to a semantically feminine girl).
The goal is to construct a detailed theory for the syntax-semantics interface of gender, enabling the explanation of gender mismatch phenomena. One central hypothesis is that gender might be described analogously to an analysis of so-called referential loci in sign languages.
Methodologically, the subproject will conduct several empirical studies to gain a solid understanding of underlying phenomena. For theory building, frameworks of dynamical semantics and DRT will be the basis.

title: P05 – The Role of Self in Pronominal Coreference
text:
Project description
Seeking for a better understanding of pronoun binding, the subproject tackles the question why cross-linguistically intensified pronouns (IntPros) tend to grammaticalize into reflexive anaphors. The hypothesis is that binding functions at the level of information structure roles: the topic binds the focus. The intensifier is the element that drives this process: a focal reflexive bound by the topic. While this is transparently the case in compositional IntPros, redundant and deficient interface operations lead both to the licensing of local rather than sentential topics as binders (see P06 for a simlar process in clitic doubling) and to the facultative interpretation of focal feature on the bindee, giving rise to vP and DP level reflexivization. Plausibly, the cycle closes with the full grammaticalization of IntPros via anaphors into reflexives, and the reemergence of fully interpreted IntPros.
In result, IntPros as the strongest pronouns do not follow the general tendency of strength regarding binding that the stronger a pronoun, the larger the structural domain in which it must be free (Cardinaletti and Starke, 1999): although strong, IntPros contain a focal reflexive, which imposes local binding by the topic. This sets the choice of target language types to Malayalam with IntPros both for intensification and as anaphors, English with IntPros mainly as anaphors, requiring additional focal pronouns for intensification, German with simple anaphors and an intensifier that strengthens their reflexivity and BCMS with simple reflexives and fully compositional IntPros. The main hypotheses directly address binding, a hallmark of R and D, as a way how grammar exploits pragmatics to economize the expressed information.

title: P10 – Deficiency and Redundancy in Expressing Temporal Relations
text:
Project description
This subproject develops a formal semantic theory of temporal pronouns and embeds it within a larger semantic model of temporal expressions, including temporal adverbials, quantifying adverbials, and aspect. Of particular interest is the temporal (sub)specification of tense features on tense morphemes and their behavior when bound by other tense forms, intensional verbs, or temporal adverbials. Focusing on these aspects allows us to directly apply the ideas on free and bound personal pronouns developed in particular in subprojects 02 and 03 to a different ontological domain, thereby testing the hypothesis that there are non-surface commonalities between pronominal systems across domains.
The investigation in this subproject is based on a comparative analysis of languages ​​with articulated tense systems such as English and German, languages ​​with articulated aspect systems such as Russian and other Slavic languages, and so-called tense-less languages ​​such as Mandarin Chinese. This subproject not only extends the empirical scope of the Collaborative Research Centre (CRC) to a new ontological domain, but also focuses centrally on Q1 by examining equilibria between the domain of meanings and a limited domain of available forms. It informs Q2 regarding binding in the temporal domain and investigates the role of syntactic structure (Q4) and feature specification (Q3) in formal semantics.

title: P08 – Fading Reference – The Pragmaticalization of Pronoun + Verb
text:
Project description
This project examines pronoun-verb combinations (prVCs), primarily in spoken Spanish and Italian. It focuses on their prototypical occurrence as content-rich predicates, their potentially grammaticalized form as discourse markers, and, most importantly, the varying degrees of fixation in intermediate forms, such as parenthetical ones. The discourse functions of prVCs formed from verbs of cognition, communication, and perception are presented, along with their dependence on pronoun types and their feature characteristics, verb type and form, the presence of other functional elements, and the syntactic positions involved. Basic grammatical operations in morphosyntax and morphophonology, as well as at the semantic-pragmatic interface, appear either to disregard the features present in the pronominal item ( R ) or to reinterpret them at the interface of language language and discourse context as different or additional pragmatic features that were not originally specified as such ( D ).
This subproject therefore investigates the influence of the feature specification of pronouns with respect to R (suppressing referential features) and D (enriching them with pragmatic features related to the language context) on the development of pronoun-related constructs (prVCs). The subproject contributes to the overarching goals of the Collaborative Research Centre (CRC) by taking a microscopic look at how the flexibility of R and D at the interfaces with phonological features (PF) and language language (LF) can be theoretically modeled to explain the potential for change and the effects of contextual linguistic and extralinguistic factors (including frequency in language use) on the grammatical system. The subproject addresses three main questions of the SFB: Q1 by focusing on grammaticalization/pragmaticalization processes as a strategy for bridging discrepancies between forms and communicative goals, Q2 by investigating the syntactic consequences of these discrepancies at the left periphery, and Q3 by investigating the feature specifications of pronouns in prVCs.

title: SFB Language between Redundancy and Deficiency
text:
Language is one of our most fundamental cognitive capacities.
This Special Research Area (SFB) Network is developing a new approach tomodeling the linguistic system. The starting point is the hypothesis that the cognitive core of language ability is based on logical-symbolic calculations, but is embedded in a cognitive system of stochastic nature. As an interface between the symbolic and stochastic components, grammar uses the central optimization factors of redundancy and deficiency, which can underlie linguistic operations and make it possible to process both under- and over-specified inputs.
The Network brings together the particularly strong linguistic research at the Universities of Graz, Vienna, and Salzburg and deals with uniformly defined, comprehensive empirical areas of grammar (pronouns and ellipsis). The sub-projects illuminate, classify and model these theoretically and empirically from the perspective of the concepts of redundancy and deficiency. Expected findings not only promise a deeper understanding of the basic mechanisms of the grammatical system, but also open up new perspectives for central questions in cognitive science regarding the role of language in cognition.
This Research Network is financed by the Austrian Science Fund for Special Research Areas (SFB Grant F1003).

He was born in Niš, Serbia, and earned his B.A. in Serbo-Croatian language and literature at the University of Niš, his M.A. in Linguistics at the University of Belgrade, and his research MA and PhD in Linguistics at the University of Leiden. title: P06 - The (Non-)Deficiency and (Non-)Redundancy of Clitic Pronouns
text:
Project description
With a focus on clitic doubling (CD), this subproject poses the fundamental question of the ontology of the domain between agreement , clitics, and weak and strong pronouns, as well as the underlying nature of the categories it contains. The strong hypothesis is that these all instantiate the same grammatical class of elements, but differ in the size of the underlying structure, as well as in the features that trigger the realization of varying degrees of strength. Hypothesizing that the answer to the latter question lies in Kiparsky’s 2008 D-hierarchy (Kallulli, 2016, 2018, 2019), and assuming universal realization of all items in the hierarchy, this subproject aims to model the strength of realization with respect to different types of D and R , including operations such as impoverishment or rules of exponentiation. In particular, the hypothesis is put forward that the feature responsible for all repeated realizations is [topic], but that it is weakened in the process of grammaticalization.
Ultimately, doubling is generalized and driven by mere syntactic locality. What begins as topic doubling in a specific position ends as agreement with the highest argument or as universal clitic doubling. Depending on various factors, primarily the degree of grammaticalization and syntactic position, languages exhibit doubling effects of varying strength, from different null elements through agreement to clitics. The main empirical questions addressed by this subproject concern binding, reconstruction effects, resumption, the person-case constraint, and (anti-)locality effects associated with clitic pronouns. The comparison of languages with and without clitics or CD regarding the underlying semantic features informs Q1 and Q3, the way in which CD influences binding relationships is relevant for Q2, and the analysis of LF and PF effects in connection with CD informs Q4.

title: P09 – Animacy Features and the Flexibility of Pronouns
text:
Project description
This subproject investigates the mapping between morphosyntactic and semantic features of French and Spanish personal pronouns from the perspective of R and D. These pronouns are highly flexible expressions due to their minimal descriptive content, and additional flexibility arises because their animacy features are not invariable (e.g., French strong pronouns are mostly used for human referents but can also refer to inanimate objects under certain conditions (Heidinger, 2019)). This subproject assumes that strong and weak pronouns are specified differently for animacy (Cardinaletti and Starke, 1999; Dobrovie-Sorin, 1999) and investigates how the animacy features of the pronouns are then manipulated by R and D to increase their flexibility and allow for non-canonical assignments (e.g., strong pronouns referring to inanimate objects).
This subproject thus investigates how repetition and diffusion enable core grammar to cope with general cognitive pressure through additional flexibility; for example, through adjustments in pronoun choice triggered by the demands of resolving anaphora. The animacy features of French and Spanish personal pronouns (especially in PPs) offer insight into the diversity and limitations of such additional flexibility. The comparative perspective of French and Spanish allows the subproject to pursue a further theoretical objective directly related to the goals of the Collaborative Research Centre (CRC): The pronoun inventories of French and Spanish both include the opposition between strong and weak pronouns. However, the languages ​​differ in the availability of weak forms in PPs. This provides an ideal testbed to examine how repetition and diffusion function in minimally different pronoun systems.

Project description
This subproject investigates clitic doubling and null objects across Spanish and Portuguese varieties, with a focus on River Plate Spanish and Mineiro Brazilian Portuguese. title: P03 – Mismatches in Binding and Coreference
text:
Project description
This project focuses on two empirical areas: fake indexicals (and other bound pronouns) and unbound pronouns that exhibit covariance. Project P03 investigates the morphological, syntactic, and semantic properties of these types of pronouns and integrates them into a model where syntax mediates between LF and PF, transferring features exhaustively or redundantly to the interfaces. It is shown that fake indexicals involve an R operation from syntax to LF, while unbound pronouns employ an R operation from syntax to PF. These two otherwise quite distinct phenomena are thus mirror images of each other within the framework of R/D of the Collaborative Research Centre (CRC).
The starting point of this subproject is a detailed syntactic investigation of pronoun structure (e.g., size and type of syntactic projections), the features involved in syntax, morphology, and semantics, any mismatches between components, and the origin of features (binding, unexpressed structures). The initial hypotheses are that i) fake indexicals involve syntactic binding through the genuine indexical , enabled by (syntactic) focus binding, and ii) that unbound pronouns are definite noun phrases in syntax that undergo an ellipsis process. This subproject is directly relevant to all the questions raised by the Collaborative Research Centre (CRC) and aims to contribute a model that allows for the formalization of the R/D mechanisms.
In addition to its theoretical focus, P03 also includes an empirical component: a detailed investigation of fake indexicals  in Romance and Slavic languages. P03 is linked—empirically and/or theoretically—to most of the other subprojects, and several collaborations have already been envisioned.

Description
The Experimental Methods cluster supports the development and exchange of methodological expertise across the project network. Its activities have included a statistics workshop, a reading group, the establishment of shared infrastructure, and the exchange of practical experience in experimental work. The cluster has also organized an online workshop on conducting online experiments and has maintained close interaction with the Romance cluster.
